notes.title: Noon ads playbook · Bid optimization: larger cuts, then bracket
notes.content:
Saved working context imported on 29 October 2026. Historical facts and examples are not current account readings. Loading this note does not authorize sends, recurring schedules or unrelated account changes. Current instructions and live API state take precedence.

## Bid optimization: larger cuts, then bracket

Keep base bids below AED 2 and preserve dynamic down and the requested boosts. Wait at least 7–8 seconds between bid-change requests/rounds; eight seconds is a preferred check interval, not verified propagation time. If results appear stale, allow further ordinary page loading rather than interpreting them as a response to the change.

1. When already first or strongly placed, lower the base. For high bids, prefer a meaningful initial cut of about AED 0.70: e.g. 1.99 to 1.29. For small bids, use a proportionate cut that respects the platform minimum (previously AED 0.25); do not subtract 0.70 blindly.
2. If the lower bid holds the position, keep it and make at most another useful bounded check. If it loses the position, bracket the last successful and unsuccessful bids and check the midpoint rather than moving a few fils repeatedly.
3. If a midpoint does not recover a previously strong position, restore the last successful bid. Avoid repeatedly chasing a volatile rank.
4. If low or absent, verify ad loading, campaign/product eligibility, stock and budget first, then make one or two bounded increases. If little useful improvement follows, return to Noon's recommended bid, capped at 1.99 and respecting the minimum, and stop. Exceptions should follow new evidence or explicit user steering, not an unbounded loop.
5. Check both SKUs; one product at #1 does not mean both are strong. Overlapping exact/phrase targets can affect attribution; do not claim a single keyword's bid uniquely caused a search-position change.

After each mutation retrieve settings and verify intended bids plus preservation of unrelated settings, products and negatives. Log previous/new bids, observations, and why a bid was lowered, restored, increased or returned to recommendation. Do not introduce a recurring monitor unless separately requested.

notes.title: Noon ads playbook · Research and target selection
notes.content:
Saved working context imported on 29 October 2026. Historical facts and examples are not current account readings. Loading this note does not authorize sends, recurring schedules or unrelated account changes. Current instructions and live API state take precedence.

## Research and target selection

1. Resolve supplied images, PSKUs, SKUs, or links to exact products. Verify price, live status, stock, fulfillment, and offer issues. Do not edit listings or unrelated campaigns.
2. Inspect previous ads for the same category: bids, match types, strategy, placements, negatives, budgets, actual customer queries, spend, clicks, ATC, orders, and revenue. Separate evidence from anecdote: one attributed order is not a proven winner. Do not copy unsuitable historical targets.
3. Use Noon keyword explorer with broad category seeds, relevant variants, and Arabic equivalents; compare monthly volume buckets. Product titles establish relevance but must not be the sole keyword source. Include genuine reported misspellings, singular/plural variants, and relevant historical purchase queries.
4. Distinguish product-specific recommendations, seed-based explorer results, and bid/volume estimates for submitted terms. Empty product recommendations do not mean the explorer is empty. Retrieve bids and demand for shortlisted terms.
5. Choose relevant demand, not popularity alone. Exclude unrelated brands, styles, product uses, and unsupported material claims. Silver-tone is not sterling/925 silver; gold-plated is not solid gold. Assess ambiguous color terms against shopper intent. Group compatible products; avoid showing incompatible products through shared targets when a better structure fits the budget.
6. Exact match provides control; add phrase selectively. State unique keyword count separately from total targets. Do not aim for a fixed count such as 19/25; that was a past example, not a requirement.

# Saved user preferences — Noon UAE

These are the user's saved operating preferences from the local Noon memories and Noon Ads skill, current through 28 October 2026. They describe preferences and historical lessons, not authorization to change the account. Current user instructions override them.

## Account control
The user requires direct API requests for all Noon account changes and does not want computer-use automation for mutations. Credentials must stay in protected server storage, not in notes, prompts, logs or exports. Read-only knowledge does not mean an account connection exists. Unrelated campaigns must not be changed, and no recurring monitoring is authorized by these preferences.

## Advertising defaults
The user prefers Manual Product Ads, dynamic down bidding (dynamic_down), top-of-search placement boost +50%, and product-page boost +25%. Base keyword bids must be strictly below AED 2: maximum AED 1.99. This restriction applies ONLY to the base bid. Placement-adjusted potential bids may exceed AED 2; do not lower base bids just to cap adjusted values at AED 2.

The preferred budget is AED 10/day average total, one combined campaign where sensible, with no end date. If more than one campaign is needed, the total average budget remains AED 10/day unless the user changes it. Average daily budgets are not strict daily or lifetime caps; never promise a hard AED 70 lifetime limit without current evidence.

## Research and targeting
The preferred workflow checks exact products, price, content/offer status, stock and fulfillment, then previous category campaigns, customer search terms, recommendations, bid evidence, and actual keyword-explorer demand. English/Arabic variants and observed misspellings matter when relevant. Titles alone are not sufficient keyword research. Exact match gives control; phrase is added selectively. There is no fixed target-count requirement. Unique keywords and total exact/phrase targets must be counted separately.

Negatives should fit the product, and conflicts must be checked. Fashion silver-tone is not sterling silver; gold-plated is not solid gold. Ring negatives must not be copied indiscriminately into earring campaigns. Existing duplicate campaigns and suitable active campaigns should be inspected before proposing a new one.

## Verification and optimization
The user expects pre-change and post-change snapshots and actual readback of strategy, products, targets, base bids, boosts, negatives, budget, dates and live/draft status. An uncertain mutation should be inspected before retrying. Campaign names are short: Brand Category | Manual | DD-MM-YYYY | w MODEL, using Asia/Dubai dates and a verified model label. Do not invent the current model identity or include "made".

Sponsored-position evidence comes from real UAE shopper results, without clicking ads, adding to carts or simulating purchases. Ad badges may be graphics. Sponsored rank and overall grid position are separate. If no sponsored cards load, a result is inconclusive. A session-specific rank does not prove a global rank, causal bid effect, profitability or the lowest possible bid.

The preferred optimization is bounded: wait at least 7–8 seconds between bid changes/rounds; for a high base bid, try a meaningful reduction around AED 0.70, proportionately smaller for low bids. If placement weakens, bracket the last successful and unsuccessful bids and check a midpoint; restore the last successful bid when appropriate. When increases fail to help, return to the recommended bid within the base cap and stop rather than chasing a volatile rank. Verify every affected SKU separately and preserve unrelated settings.

## Catalog lesson
An earlier account audit found standalone Apple Watch bands incorrectly assigned to fashion watch-strap taxonomy. The verified intended category then was Electronic Accessories → Wearables → Smartwatch Band, with code electronic_accessories-wearables-smartwatch_band. Case-and-band bundles and other product types need separate checks. This is a historical lesson, not permission for a bulk edit. Canonical display SKUs and original partner_sku values may differ; content updates must resolve the original identifiers and verify actual taxonomy readback.

A customer return, a refund, a dispute and a return-to-vendor request are distinct operations. Procedures differ between FBP and FBN. Identify the order, item, reason, fulfillment model, received condition and relevant deadlines before proposing a resolution. Use the current program policy for timeframes rather than mixing them across programs.

For FBP, seller evaluation and evidence can affect resolution, while a return remains a tracked process. For FBN, returned stock and QC status determine whether units return to saleable inventory or require a different path. Do not promise compensation or claim a dispute is approved without an actual result. Changes affecting refunds, disposal, RTV or customer communications need explicit authorization and evidence.

# Noon · Inventory ledgers, receiving and reconciliation

Inventory ledgers provide summary and detailed views of stock movement. Use the correct report to distinguish a closing balance from the movements that produced it. Receiving/GRN evidence, sales, returns, adjustments and removals are different events and should be reconciled using matching identifiers, warehouses and dates.

For a discrepancy, compare opening stock plus receipts and returns, less fulfilled units and removals, with recorded adjustments and closing stock. Confirm how the report defines each column before applying a formula. Do not treat a recommendation for replenishment or RTV as an executed movement. Preserve report exports and investigate the period with supporting evidence; unresolved differences belong in Seller Support rather than being hidden by an unverified stock edit.

In Seller Lab, Catalog → My Catalog exposes product records and their offer/visibility status. Product identity, product content, and offer details are distinct. Titles, images, descriptions, attributes, brand and taxonomy describe the product. A parent/variant relationship groups appropriate sizes or colors; an offer describes the seller's price, stock and commercial terms.

Resolve the exact seller SKU/PSKU and Noon identifier before proposing an edit. Check parent/child relationships, taxonomy, mandatory attributes, moderation/content status, offer status, stock and fulfillment separately. Fixing content does not prove an offer is live. Never infer material claims such as sterling silver or solid gold from color alone. Preserve original identifiers during readback and verify any change in the correct content and offer views.

# Noon · Seller Lab sections and navigation

Seller Lab is the operational workspace for a Noon seller. Start with the store dashboard for sales, units, visibility, and urgent operational tasks. Catalog manages product content and offers. Fulfillment and inventory depend on FBN versus FBP. Orders, returns, finance, reports, and advertising answer different questions; do not treat them as interchangeable.

Choose the section from the task: a wrong title or category belongs to catalog content; unavailable stock belongs to inventory/offers; a shipment issue belongs to fulfillment/orders; campaign spend belongs to ads; payout reconciliation belongs to finance. Menu labels and availability can vary by country, program, and account access. A guide does not establish that this app is connected to the seller account.
